item.text: The app uses Next’s App Router with plain `Link`s and server-rendered pages. I’m adding a small client navigation layer so a route update happens inside the browser’s View Transition API, then matching the thumbnail and hero by product slug. I’ll keep a CSS fallback for browsers without that API and disable both route and skeleton motion under reduced motion.

The transition plumbing and shared image names are in place. I’m reviewing the generated diff now for React/Next event handling and CSS selector compatibility, especially the reduced-motion path and the Suspense reveal.

item.text: The gallery thumbnail and detail hero now use the same per-product transition name. Internal gallery/back links run their route update through a persistent client wrapper, which lets the browser capture both pages and slide them in opposite directions. Suspense fallback/content also use short entrance fades, with the reduced-motion media query disabling those effects. I’m doing a final diff sanity check; I’m leaving the pre-existing package manifest changes untouched.

item.text:
Implemented browser View Transitions for gallery navigation. Product thumbnails and detail heroes share a per-product transition name, and gallery/back navigation slides in opposite directions. Suspense fallback and loaded content fade in, and reduced-motion preferences disable the animations.

The navigation wrapper is in [NavigationTransitions.tsx](/workspace/app/NavigationTransitions.tsx). I also updated [ProductGrid.tsx](/workspace/app/ProductGrid.tsx), [page.tsx](/workspace/app/product/[slug]/page.tsx), [layout.tsx](/workspace/app/layout.tsx), and [globals.css](/workspace/app/globals.css).

`git diff --check` passed. I did not run a build or tests. I left the existing `package.json` changes and untracked `package-lock.json` untouched.
